question.problem: Find the values of $k$ for which the quadratic equation $-15{x}^{2}+kx-60=0$  has one distinct real solution.
question.worked_solution:
The equation has one distinct real solution if its discriminant is zero. So, we need to find the values of $k$ so that the discriminant is zero.

First, we calculate the discriminant. We have $a=-15,$ $b=k,$ and $c=-60,$ so the discriminant is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={b}^{2}-4ac \\  & =(k)^{2}-4(-15)(-60) \\  & ={k}^{2}-3\,600\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the values of $k$ such that the discriminant is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=0 \\ {k}^{2}-3600 & =0 \\ {k}^{2} & =3600 \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{3600} \\ k & =\pm 60\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the given equation will have one distinct real solution if $k=\pm 60.$
